experiments.verification_evidence: Rendered page 7 (PDF page 7 of 12; pdfinfo reports Pages: 12) shows Table III directly below Table II caption. Table III spans printed rows from 'TIRG [5]' to 'Baseline | BLIP2 | - | 48.04 72.65 | 53.54 73.91 | 57.37 78.85 | 52.98 75.13 | 64.07' and 'PTHA (Ours) | BLIP2 | - | 49.54 72.81 | 55.50 73.97 | 57.96 78.96 | 54.33 75.24 | 64.79', then the paper's FashionIQ row 'PTHA (Ours) | BLIP2 | FashionIQMTST | 50.77 73.78 | 55.91 75.36 | 58.28 79.70 | 54.99 76.28 | 65.64'. The registry's 54.99 / 76.28 / 65.64 matches this row exactly and matches no other row (the closest non-MTST PTHA row is 54.33 / 75.24 / 64.79 and SPRC is 54.92 / 74.97 / 64.85), so the registry is not reading a competitor row or a no-pretraining row. GALLERY PROTOCOL CAVEAT, stated explicitly: the PAPER does not state its gallery construction or reference policy - the only protocol sentence is 'For FashionIQ, we report the R@10 and R@50 on the val set in three categories'. The protocol recorded here is therefore a SOURCE-DERIVED reading of the authors' own published evaluator (https://github.com/zyinan99/MTST_PTHA, un-pinned upstream main HEAD 6a02ee4763fc2260b6abfb18be78853facb91d86), NOT a paper statement: data_utils.py:165-168 builds the gallery by json.load of image_splits/split.{cat}.val.json in file order (full split, one category per dataset instance), utils.py:54-55 iterates it with DataLoader(batch_size=64, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True, collate_fn=collate_fn) with NO shuffle argument, and validate_blip.py:44-51 compares sorted_index_names against np.repeat(target_names, len(index_names)) with no reference mask anywhere on the FashionIQ path (the CIRR path does build a reference_mask, at validate_blip.py:258-260 and :331-333, proving the omission on the FIQ path is deliberate). That combination is exactly workbench protocol fashioniq_original_split (src/evaluation/fashioniq.py:172-174: gallery='full_split', reference_excluded=False). Local dataset confirms the gallery is well formed for that protocol: dress gallery 3817 / queries 2017, shirt 6346 / 2038, toptee 5373 / 1961, all gallery ids unique within their category, every reference and every target present in its gallery, ref==target count 0 in all three - so the assert at validate_blip.py:51 (exactly one hit per query) would hold. experiments.verification_method: Two independent routes that agree, plus an arithmetic check. (1) HTML route: curl https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05316v1 (HTML 200, 303805 B), parsed the 12th <table> on the page row-by-row with a Python regex/HTML unescape script; every cell of the last row read 50.77 | 73.78 | 55.91 | 75.36 | 58.28 | 79.70 | 54.99 | 76.28 | 65.64. (2) PDF route: pdftotext -layout paper.pdf paper.txt, the same row at lines 465-466 of paper.txt with identical values and column alignment. (3) Visual route: pdftoppm -f 7 -l 7 -r 160 -png paper.pdf then read page7-07.png as an image; the Table III last row visibly reads PTHA (Ours) / BLIP2 / FashionIQ_MTST / 50.77 73.78 / 55.91 75.36 / 58.28 79.70 / 54.99 76.28 / 65.64, with 'FashionIQMTST' in subscript shading. All three routes agree on every digit. (4) Arithmetic: category macro means recomputed as (50.77+55.91+58.28)/3 = 54.9867 -> 54.99 and (73.78+75.36+79.70)/3 = 76.28; (54.99+76.28)/2 = 65.635 -> 65.64, matching the printed Average and Avg. columns, so the printed averages are internally consistent and are not a per-category value.
